{{inline |date=May 2024}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Bombieri norm''', named after [[Enrico Bombieri]], is a [[Norm (mathematics)|norm]] on [[homogeneous polynomial]]s with coefficient in <math>\mathbb R</math> or <math>\mathbb C</math> (there is also a version for non homogeneous univariate polynomials). This norm has many remarkable properties, the most important being listed in this article.

==Bombieri scalar product for homogeneous polynomials==

To start with the geometry, the ''Bombieri scalar product'' for [[homogeneous polynomial]]s with ''N'' variables can be defined as follows using [[multi-index notation]]:<math display="block">\forall \alpha,\beta \in \mathbb{N}^N</math>
by definition different monomials are orthogonal, so that
<math display="block">\langle X^\alpha | X^\beta \rangle = 0</math> if <math>\alpha \neq \beta,</math>

while <math display="block">\forall \alpha \in \mathbb{N}^N</math> by definition <math display="block">\|X^\alpha\|^2 = \frac{\alpha!}{|\alpha|!}.</math>

In the above definition and in the rest of this article the following notation applies:

if <math display="block">\alpha = (\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_N) \in \mathbb{N}^N,</math> write <math display="block">|\alpha| = \sum_{i=1}^N \alpha_i</math> and <math display="block">\alpha! = \prod_{i=1}^N (\alpha_i!)</math> and <math display="block">X^\alpha = \prod_{i=1}^N X_i^{\alpha_i}.</math>

==Bombieri inequality==
The fundamental property of this norm is the Bombieri inequality:

let <math>P,Q</math> be two homogeneous polynomials respectively of degree <math>d^\circ(P)</math> and <math>d^\circ(Q)</math> with <math>N</math> variables, then, the following inequality holds:

:<math>\frac{d^\circ(P)!d^\circ(Q)!}{(d^\circ(P)+d^\circ(Q))!}\|P\|^2 \, \|Q\|^2 \leq 
 \|P\cdot Q\|^2 \leq \|P\|^2 \, \|Q\|^2.</math>

Here the Bombieri inequality is the left hand side of the above statement, while the right side means that the Bombieri norm is an [[algebra norm]]. Giving the left hand side is meaningless without that constraint, because in this case, we can achieve the same result with any norm by multiplying the norm by a well chosen factor.

This multiplicative inequality implies that the product of two polynomials is bounded from below by a quantity that depends on the multiplicand polynomials. Thus, this product can not be arbitrarily small. This multiplicative inequality is useful in metric [[algebraic geometry]] and [[number theory]].

==Invariance by isometry==
Another important property is that the Bombieri norm is invariant by composition with an 
[[isometry]]:

let <math>P,Q</math> be two homogeneous polynomials of degree <math>d</math> with <math>N</math> variables and let <math>h</math> be an isometry
of <math>\mathbb R^N</math> (or <math>\mathbb C^N</math>). Then we have <math>\langle P\circ h|Q\circ h\rangle = \langle P|Q\rangle</math>. When <math>P=Q</math> this implies <math>\|P\circ h\|=\|P\|</math>.

This result follows from a nice integral formulation of the scalar product:

: <math>\langle P|Q\rangle = {d+N-1 \choose N-1} \int_{S^N} P(Z)\overline{Q(Z)}\,d\sigma(Z)</math>

where <math>S^N</math> is the unit sphere of <math>\mathbb C^N</math> with its canonical measure <math>d\sigma(Z)</math>.

==Other inequalities==
Let <math>P</math> be a homogeneous polynomial of degree <math>d</math> with <math>N</math> variables and let <math>Z \in \mathbb C^N</math>. We have:

* <math>|P(Z)| \leq \|P\| \, \|Z\|_E^d</math>
* <math>\|\nabla P(Z)\|_E \leq d \|P\| \, \|Z\|_E^d</math>

where <math>\|\cdot\|_E</math> denotes the Euclidean norm.

The Bombieri norm is useful in polynomial factorization, where it has some advantages over the [[Mahler measure]], according to Knuth.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Knuth |first=Donald Ervin |author-link=Donald Knuth |title=[[The Art of Computer Programming]] |date=1997 |publisher=Addison-Wesley |isbn=978-0-201-89683-1 |edition=3rd |location=Reading, Mass |pages=457-458, 682-684}}</ref>
